title: How to copy zoom invite link on mac: scheduled and live meetings in Zoom Workplace
metaTitle: How to Copy Zoom Invite Link on Mac (Step by Step)
description: How to copy Zoom invite link on Mac: copy a scheduled meeting or a live one, use ⌘⇧I, and turn on auto-copy in Zoom Workplace.
targetKeyword: how to copy zoom invite link on mac
intro: To copy a Zoom invite link on Mac, open a scheduled meeting in Zoom Workplace, click More, and choose Copy invitation, which includes the join link. During a live meeting, click Participants, then Invite, and select Copy invite link in the bottom-left corner or press ⌘⇧I.
tldr: Scheduled meeting: open it, click More, then choose Copy invitation. That copies the full text with the join link.
Live meeting: click Participants, then Invite, then Copy invite link in the bottom-left corner.
Shortcut: ⌘⇧I copies the invite link during a meeting. ⌘I opens the invite window.
Paste with ⌘V. If the option is missing, check whether the meeting has started.

blocks.text: Zoom gives you two different copy options, and most of the confusion comes from mixing them up. One copies a short invite link. The other copies the full invitation text, including the join link. This guide covers both in the Zoom Workplace desktop app on a Mac. Zoom's help pages give the same steps for Windows and Linux. The Mac-specific parts are the ⌘ shortcuts and pasting with ⌘V.
Copy the invite link for a scheduled meeting

A scheduled meeting is one you set up ahead of time. It sits on your calendar in Zoom Workplace, and you can copy its invitation before anyone joins. Start from the Calendar tab. Click the meeting, and a pop-up opens with the options for that meeting.

The option you want sits in the top-right corner of that pop-up, under More. Choose Copy invitation. Scheduled meetings don't show Copy invite link, so don't spend time looking for it there. That option only appears once the meeting is running.

You can also start from the Home tab. Upcoming meetings show up as cards there. Click a card to see the join link under Join Zoom Meeting, and copy that link directly. The ellipsis on the card offers Copy invitation too. Use the bare link when a form only wants a URL. Use Copy invitation when you want a message with context.
Example: a project review you send ahead of time

Say you schedule a project review for next week. Open it from Calendar, click More, and choose Copy invitation. Paste the message into your email thread with ⌘V. Your colleagues get one message with the join link, so nobody has to ask for it.
Copy the invite link during a live meeting

When the meeting is running, the invite tools move into the meeting window. Start with Participants. Click it in the meeting controls. If the Invite window doesn't open by itself, this is how you reach it. At the bottom of the Participants panel, click Invite.

The Invite window has two copy options. Copy invite link sits in the bottom-left corner, and it copies the link alone. Copy invitation gives you the full text. Pick the one that matches what the person on the other end needs.

blocks.text: Copy invitation sits in the same Invite window, so you don't need to switch to the calendar during a call. The window is the one place where both options live side by side.
Example: a late guest in a running meeting

A guest is running late, and the call has already started. Click Participants, then Invite at the bottom of the panel. Click Copy invite link, switch to the chat, and press ⌘V. The guest joins from that link without waiting for a new invitation.
Use keyboard shortcuts for the invite link

Zoom's hot keys article lists three Meetings shortcuts for macOS. ⌘I opens the invite window. ⌘⇧I copies the invite link. ⌘U shows or hides the Participants panel. These help most when your hands stay on the keyboard during a call.
Watch the chat shortcut. Shift+Command+U is a separate, chat-only shortcut. Pressing it won't open Participants. If ⌘U seems broken, check that you didn't add Shift by accident.

Zoom says shortcuts can be edited in the desktop app settings. Some can be set as global, which lets them work when Zoom is not in focus. Open Keyboard shortcuts to see the defaults. The Restore button puts the defaults back if you change something by mistake.
Turn on automatic copying for the invite link

If you invite people all day, you can let Zoom do the copying. Zoom has a setting called Automatically copy invite link to clipboard. It sits under Meetings & webinars, in the In-meeting and in-webinar experience section. Turn it on, and the link goes to your clipboard for you.

Zoom's article doesn't say which way this setting starts, so check the box yourself and confirm it is on. Auto-copy writes to the same clipboard as ⌘C. Whatever was written last is what ⌘V pastes. Paste what you need first.
Copy the invite link from the web portal

If the app is closed or you're on another computer, use the web portal. Sign in and open Meetings. Choose the Upcoming tab, then click the meeting topic. Click Copy Invitation, then Copy Meeting Invitation. The copy icon beside Invite Link works too, if you only need the link.

The web portal filters by date. A meeting outside the selected date range won't show up. Change the time range field until the meeting appears, then copy as normal. People often search the list, find nothing, and assume the meeting is gone.
Why the copy option is missing

Most missing options have a simple cause. Copy invite link only shows during a meeting. For a scheduled meeting, use More, then Copy invitation. If that isn't enough, the Invite window may not have opened. Click Participants, then Invite.

University of Minnesota IT gives the same advice. Its guide says Copy Invite Link appears only for a meeting in progress, and scheduled meetings use Copy Invitation. Zoom's invite article lists the same split.

Some third-party guides say a missing option means you aren't the host, or that attendee sharing is off. Zoom's official pages don't confirm that rule. If the option stays missing, ask the host of the meeting to check the settings.

Email invites are a separate issue. Zoom says email invites need calendar and contacts integration. The Only show default email setting can remove the Gmail and Yahoo options from the Invite window. Those email options are not the copy buttons, so you can still copy the link.
Mistakes that send the wrong link

The first mistake is copying the wrong option for the meeting type. A scheduled meeting needs Copy invitation. A live meeting needs Copy invite link. Mixing them up sends people hunting for an option that isn't there.

The second mistake is pasting a full invitation into a field that wants only a URL. The message is long and the link gets buried. Use Copy invite link, or the link under the Home tab card, when a form asks for a link.
The third mistake is the clipboard. Auto-copy and manual copy write to the same clipboard. Whatever you copied last is what ⌘V pastes. Copy again right before you paste.
The fourth mistake is assuming a shortcut works from any app. Zoom says some shortcuts can be set as global. Check your Keyboard shortcuts list before you rely on one during a call.
What the Basic plan limits mean for shared links

Zoom's pricing page lists the Basic plan at 40 minutes per meeting and 100 participants per meeting. Those limits apply to the meeting itself. The pricing page doesn't say invite links change them, so don't assume they do.

If your group needs longer calls, compare plans on the pricing page before the meeting. A 40 minute limit can cut off a long discussion. Plan the agenda around that number, or set up the meeting on a plan that fits. For scheduling steps, see [how to schedule a Zoom meeting on Mac](/how-to/schedule-a-meeting-in-zoom).
What to do after you copy the link
Paste with ⌘V into an email, chat or calendar note. Copy invitation pastes the whole message, so you can send it as it is. Read the message once before you send it. Check that the join link is there.

items: Copied from the right meeting, not an older one.
Pasted with ⌘V, then read before sending.
Sent the invitation itself, not a screenshot of it.
Joined once from another device to test the link.

blocks.text: Test the link before a big call. Join from your phone or another computer. If it opens the meeting, the link works. If you're still learning how joining works, read [how to join a Zoom meeting on Mac](/how-to/join-a-meeting-in-zoom).
Check your version before you follow menus

Zoom updated the desktop interface in version 6.7.0. If your menus look different, check your version first. Click your profile picture, then Settings. On 6.7.0 or later, the gear icon in the navigation bar opens Settings as well.

Zoom's release notes list macOS builds 7.2.5 from October 31, 2026, 7.2.2 from September 24, 2026, and 7.2.1 from September 21, 2026. None of those notes changes the invite link, Copy invitation or the Invite window on macOS. If you're behind, see [how to update Zoom on Mac](/how-to/update-zoom-in-zoom).

faq.question: Where is Copy invite link on Mac?
faq.answer: It sits in the bottom-left corner of the Invite window during a live meeting. Open Participants, click Invite at the bottom of the panel, then click Copy invite link. It doesn't appear for scheduled meetings.

faq.question: What is the Zoom shortcut to copy an invite link on Mac?
faq.answer: ⌘⇧I copies the invite link during a meeting, according to Zoom's hot keys article. ⌘I opens the invite window. You can edit shortcuts in Settings under Keyboard shortcuts, and Restore brings back the defaults.

faq.question: Why can't I find Copy invite link for a scheduled meeting?
faq.answer: Copy invite link only shows while a meeting is running. For a scheduled meeting, open it, click More in the top-right corner, and choose Copy invitation.

faq.question: Does Copy invitation include the join link?
faq.answer: Yes. Zoom describes it as the full invitation text, and the join link is part of it. Paste it with ⌘V into your email or chat.

faq.question: Can I copy an invite link from the web portal?
faq.answer: Yes. Go to Meetings, open the Upcoming tab, click the meeting topic, then click Copy Invitation and Copy Meeting Invitation. Use the copy icon beside Invite Link if you only need the link.

faq.question: Why are the Gmail and Yahoo options missing?
faq.answer: Email invites need calendar and contacts integration. The Only show default email setting can remove those options from the Invite window. The copy buttons are separate from those email options.

faq.question: Does the Basic plan change how invite links work?
faq.answer: Zoom's pricing page lists 40 minutes per meeting and 100 participants per meeting on the Basic plan. The page doesn't say invite links change those limits. Check the pricing page if you're unsure.

steps.name: Open Zoom Workplace and sign in
steps.text: Open Zoom Workplace from the Dock or the Applications folder, then sign in. You need to be signed in to see your scheduled meetings.

steps.name: Open the meeting from Calendar
steps.text: Click the Calendar tab in the left navigation. Find the meeting and click it to open its pop-up. The Calendar side panel shows similar options when you click the ellipsis on an event.
steps.tip: If your version labels this area Meetings, use that tab. Zoom's articles name both, so check your screen.

steps.name: Click More in the pop-up
steps.text: In the top-right corner of the meeting pop-up, click More. The menu opens with the invitation options for that meeting.

steps.name: Choose Copy invitation
steps.text: Click Copy invitation. Zoom copies the full invitation text, including the join link, to your clipboard.

steps.name: Paste the invitation with ⌘V
steps.text: Switch to your email, chat or calendar and press ⌘V. Read the message before you send it so the join link is easy to find.

steps.name: Start or join the meeting as host
steps.text: Open the meeting in Zoom. Copy invite link appears only while the meeting is running, so start the call first.
steps.tip: Scheduled meetings keep using Copy invitation, even after the call starts.

steps.name: Open the Participants panel
steps.text: Click Participants in the meeting controls. If the Invite window already opened, skip this step. Otherwise, Participants is the route to the Invite window.

steps.name: Click Invite at the bottom of the panel
steps.text: At the bottom of the Participants panel, click Invite. Choose your options, then click Invite to open the Invite window.

steps.name: Click Copy invite link
steps.text: In the Invite window, click Copy invite link in the bottom-left corner. It copies only the link, not the full invitation text.
steps.tip: Need the full text instead? Click Copy invitation in the same window.

steps.name: Paste the link with ⌘V
steps.text: Switch to the chat or email where you want the link, press ⌘V, and send it. Send it while the meeting is still running so people can join.

steps.name: Turn on automatic copying
steps.text: Open Settings from your profile picture. Click Meetings & webinars, then find In-meeting and in-webinar experience. Turn on Automatically copy invite link to clipboard.
steps.tip: On version 6.7.0 or later, the gear icon in the navigation bar also opens Settings.

steps.name: Check or change a shortcut
steps.text: In Settings, open Keyboard shortcuts to see the defaults. Edit a shortcut in the list if you want a different key. Click Restore to return to the defaults.

troubleshooting.problem: No Copy invite link option anywhere
troubleshooting.fix: It only shows during a meeting that is running. For a scheduled meeting, click More and choose Copy invitation.

troubleshooting.problem: The Invite window does not open
troubleshooting.fix: Click Participants in the meeting controls, then click Invite at the bottom of the panel.
Make sure Zoom is in focus. Check Settings under Keyboard shortcuts in case the key was changed, and click Restore to bring back the defaults.

troubleshooting.problem: Gmail or Yahoo options are missing from the Invite window
troubleshooting.fix: Email invites need calendar and contacts integration. Check the Only show default email setting, since it can remove those options.

troubleshooting.problem: A scheduled meeting does not appear on the web portal
troubleshooting.fix: Change the time range field. Meetings outside the selected date range do not appear.
The last thing copied is what ⌘V pastes. Copy again right before you paste, especially with auto-copy turned on.
